subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by the shared fenced reply-session-init self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or should maintainers require explicit WebChat/heartbeat retry parity before treating it as fixed?
rationale: Current source shows both a shared conflict throw and surface-level terminalization paths; the permanent owner boundary affects whether OpenClaw fixes this in session lifecycle recovery or by adding separate retry loops to each inbound surface.

options.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical fix path, then validate WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands before adding surface-specific retry loops.

options.title: Require Surface Retry Parity
options.body: Keep the shared PR separate and require WebChat and heartbeat to classify reply-session-init conflicts as retryable regardless of shared session recovery.

options.title: Ask For One More Live Surface Proof
options.body: Request a focused current-main live reproduction or patched validation for WebChat or heartbeat before choosing the repair layer.

recommendation.title: Review Shared Self-Heal First
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 as the canonical fix path, then validate WebChat and heartbeat conflict behavior after it lands before adding surface-specific retry loops.

likelyOwner.reason: jalehman has the strongest recent merged history on the guarded reply-session initialization and session-accessor boundary where the owner-boundary choice sits.
